name: Timeline
blurb: How motion design got here, from Fantasmagorie to real-time — because the field did not start with After Effects.

entries.name: Émile Cohl, Fantasmagorie
entries.note: Widely treated as the first fully animated film — drawn line, no photography of objects.

entries.name: Walther Ruttmann and Viking Eggeling
entries.note: Abstract film in Germany: motion as composition rather than as story.

entries.name: Oskar Fischinger
entries.note: Visual music. Shape and colour cut to sound, decades before anyone said "motion graphics".

entries.name: Len Lye, direct animation
entries.note: Painting and scratching straight onto film stock. The first camera-less motion design.

entries.name: Norman McLaren at the NFB
entries.note: Drawn sound, pixilation, and a lifetime of technique invented per film.

entries.name: Saul Bass, title sequences
entries.note: Title design becomes authored work — Anatomy of a Murder, Vertigo, North by Northwest.

entries.name: Pablo Ferro
entries.note: Fast-cut, hand-lettered titles. Dr. Strangelove set the template for kinetic type.

entries.name: John Whitney, analogue computing
entries.note: Mechanical computers driving film cameras. The direct ancestor of procedural motion.

entries.name: MTV launches
entries.note: A whole channel of identity design. Motion graphics becomes an industry with clients.

entries.name: Adobe Photoshop ships
entries.note: The raster foundation everything else in the pipeline assumed.

entries.name: CoSA After Effects 1.0
entries.note: Compositing and keyframing on a desktop. The tool that defined the job title.

entries.name: Cinema 4D on desktop
entries.note: Accessible 3D for designers, and later MoGraph — procedural motion without scripting.

entries.name: Kyle Cooper, Se7en titles
entries.note: Title design as graphic authorship again, and the start of the modern title sequence.

entries.name: The Matrix and bullet time
entries.note: Effects language leaks into commercial motion work for a decade.

entries.name: Motionographer founded
entries.note: The field gets a public record, a critical voice, and a job board.

entries.name: Vimeo becomes the reel
entries.note: Portfolio distribution moves from showreels on tape to a public URL.

entries.name: Blender goes open source
entries.note: A free, complete 3D pipeline. Two decades later it is a real production option.

entries.name: School of Motion opens
entries.note: Structured motion education outside universities. Bootcamps, cohorts, feedback.

entries.name: Lottie released
entries.note: Vector animation ships into apps at any resolution. UI motion becomes a discipline.

entries.name: Rive and real-time motion
entries.note: Interactive, state-driven animation designed once and run live in product.

entries.name: Real-time and generative
entries.note: Unreal, TouchDesigner and shader work move from experiment to client deliverable.

entries.name: Generative AI arrives
entries.note: The tools change weekly. Judgement, taste and direction become the scarce part.
